system:
Resolve reference/request licences for each visual attribute. Return only governs and reasons matching the supplied JSON contract. Interpret the complete request semantically, without keyword lists. The separate medium_decision already settles rendering-medium permission and taxonomy: the medium owner is pinned by the schema. Host code computes the style phrase, transformation phrase/target, discrepancy and note from the accepted medium decision. Do not return those host-owned fields.
With no visual reference, every visual attribute is request-governed. Otherwise the reference governs every attribute the user has not actually specified. Explicit requests outrank observed references, and references outrank director notes. A director only fills unresolved space. Source metadata, target aspect, duration and creativity are not instructions about camera framing, lighting, wardrobe, palette or rendering process. A stale Asset.Description is caller commentary; actual Card observations govern reference appearance. Independent reference_readings are real supplied readings even when this analysis attaches no conditioning media.
Action: a requested new action or performed behavior overrides a subject plate's static pose, including an explicit vocal performance or speaking action. Action authority concerns what the figure is asked to do, not only locomotion; a performance request does not need physical travel. An intelligible requested behavior remains an action when the caller uses imperfect tense, inflection or grammar; do not claim no action merely because the sentence is ungrammatical. Merely changing which figure performs an existing source action does not itself change that action. Wardrobe: a requested clothing/accessory change overrides only the named properties; otherwise retain the corresponding figure's observed clothes. Framing: an actual requested camera composition, shot scale, viewpoint or movement governs; merely being somewhere, moving in a direction or choosing a canvas ratio does not. Lighting: an instruction about the light, an illuminating source, its direction or its visible quality governs. Placement under an illuminating practical source therefore governs that light; weather, time of day, location, an object whose name implies a time, and mood alone do not authorize replacing reference lighting. Palette includes the scene's color and tonal grading, saturation and contrast treatment. An explicit requested grade/tonal contrast therefore governs palette even without a new hue. An object's incidental color does not recolor or regrade the scene.
In an edit, the edit_source clip owns the scene's observed appearance before incoming identity portraits. Incoming replacement/placement images supply identity; their studio lighting/backdrop must not replace the clip's world. For a non-frame content reference, sheet panels, labels, multiple views and posing are presentation, not the new scene or identity. For actual_frame sources, the entire supplied image is the target frame at its anchored instant: preserve those pixels, including their complete layout and source background. Never authorize sheet cleanup on an actual frame merely because it is a sheet. An observed pose is licensed only for an actual frame anchor, never as an identity attribute. Keep rendering restyling independent of retention relationship: changing a medium does not itself select attribute_transfer.
Target identities are already resolved by identity_requirements. Those are TARGET descriptors and properties after explicit caller requirements; original observed_subjects remain the SOURCE. Do not reassert a conflicting source gender/species/age/wardrobe as a request error. Neither re-author those identity decisions nor return identity fields. Resolve only the remaining attribute owners and their reasons.

brief.intent: the woman in the technical jacket rides the dragon into an epic battleground, cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements

cards.summary: A cinematic character reference sheet titled HERO for an adult character in black tactical clothing. A large rainy night street portrait is followed by full-body front, side-profile, and back views and close-up detail panels of the face, jacket collar, hands, and boots.

subjects.descriptor: adult character labeled HERO, shown across multiple reference views
attributes: short undercut hairstyle with longer hair gathered at the top/back
black tactical jacket with chest strap and metal buckle
dark crew-neck shirt
black cargo trousers
black lace-up combat boots
pose: Top hero image: stands with arms at sides and head turned toward the viewer's left
Front panel: faces camera with arms at sides
Side profile panel: stands in left-facing profile
Back panel: faces away with arms at sides
Face panel: neutral, serious expression directed toward camera

cards.environment: Top panel: rainy nighttime urban walkway with metal railings and out-of-focus city lights. Lower panels: dark grey seamless studio background.
cards.lighting: Low-key cinematic lighting; the top night scene has cool blue-grey rain tones and warm amber street-light bokeh, while the reference panels use soft directional studio light with deep shadows.
cards.framing: Composite character reference layout: a large top hero image, a middle row of three full-body panels, and a bottom row of four close-up detail panels.
cards.style: Photorealistic cinematic character reference sheet with a dark, gritty, rainy neo-noir aesthetic.

cards.summary: A dark fantasy dragon character reference sheet: one large atmospheric side-view hero panel above a grid of three full-body turnaround views (front, side profile, rear) and four close-up detail panels (head, wing membrane, claw and foot, scale detail).

subjects.descriptor: Large black dragon with ivory horns, spiked spine, membranous wings, and long tail
attributes: dark charcoal-black scales with subtle blue-grey iridescence
long pale ivory horns swept back from the head
row of spikes along neck and spine
large membranous wings with bony fingers and veined texture
long spiked tail
quadrupedal stance with clawed feet and pale curved claws
amber eye in the head close-up
pose: standing in side profile with head lowered in the hero panel
wings spread in the front and rear views
wings folded along the body in the side profile view

subjects.descriptor: Dark rocky fantasy terrain with misty sky and faint ember glow
attributes: jagged dark rock formations
misty grey sky
faint orange ember-like glow near the ground on the right
neutral dark grey backdrop behind the turnaround and detail panels

cards.environment: Dark, moody fantasy landscape of black rock and mist in the hero panel; the reference panels use a plain dark grey backdrop.
cards.lighting: Low-key, moody lighting with cool grey highlights on the scales and horns, plus dim orange ember glow in the hero background.
cards.framing: Wide landscape image divided into a large top hero panel and a lower grid of seven smaller reference panels.
cards.style: Dark fantasy creature concept art, highly detailed photorealistic rendering in a reference-sheet layout.

rendering_permission.reasoning: The mention of a “cinematic hollywood scene with dramatic expressions and camera movements” is a descriptive style tag appended to the scene action, not an explicit rendering transformation or a grammatical instruction specifying a complete target rendition. No authorizing operation or target rendition is stated.

medium_decision.retained_style: Photorealistic cinematic with a dark, gritty, rainy neo-noir aesthetic
medium_decision.reasoning: The rendering_permission is preserve, so the source look remains anchored. The first observed reference style is a photorealistic cinematic character reference sheet with a dark, gritty, rainy neo-noir aesthetic; because it is a content reference sheet, only the sheet/presentation packaging is removed from retained_style, leaving the actual visual style. The request describes an epic cinematic scene with dramatic expressions and camera movement, but does not explicitly name a rendering medium or a complete requested rendering noun phrase. Therefore requested_medium and requested_style remain empty, while cinematic and dramatic are recorded as requested treatments.
